title: When the Lantern Sings
premise: In the river town of Anshui on the eve of revolution, Xanthe Zhou passes as a boy in his father's print shop, carving typefaces and keeping his head down. When imperial troops requisition the town, they seize the shop's ledgers—records that could expose deserters, smugglers, and Xanthe's own hidden identity. As winter closes in and the army hunts the ledger's keeper, Xanthe must ally with a disgraced soldier and a lantern-maker's widow to steal it back. The story ends at the frozen river's edge, where one berth remains on the last boat before the ice breaks, and Xanthe chooses to give it to his ailing father while he stays behind to lead the town's hidden families through the thaw.
about_author: Sebastian Vane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing provincial printing records from the late imperial era. He writes historical fiction about ordinary people caught in the machinery of upheaval.

chapters.title: The Smell of Ink and Iron
chapters.summary: Xanthe Zhou, presenting as a young man, works the type cases in his family's print shop while soldiers drill across the river. His father coughs blood into a rag; his sister Mei keeps their secret. POV: Xanthe. Beat: quiet dread beneath routine—the war is close enough to smell.

chapters.title: Names in Lead
chapters.summary: A customer asks Xanthe to print pamphlets for reformers; his father refuses, but Xanthe secretly sets the type at night. Mei catches him and covers for him. POV: Xanthe. Beat: first small act of defiance, thrilling and terrifying.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Imperial troops march into Anshui and commandeer the print shop as a garrison office. Captain Ruan demands all ledgers of names—residents, debts, loyalties. The Zhou ledger holds records that could doom half the town. POV: Xanthe. Beat: the safe world ends in an afternoon.

chapters.title: The Widow of Lantern Row
chapters.summary: Xanthe seeks help from Auntie Sable, a lantern-maker whose son was executed years ago; she knows every tunnel under the town. She agrees to hide the copied pages but warns him trust is a debt with interest. POV: Xanthe. Beat: found family begins to form.

chapters.title: A Soldier Who Reads
chapters.summary: Corporal Deng, a conscript assigned to inventory the shop, discovers Xanthe copying the ledger and says nothing. Their wary conversation reveals Deng deserted once before and was caught. POV: alternating Xanthe/Deng. Beat: enemy becomes ambiguous ally.

chapters.title: The First Frost
chapters.summary: Rations tighten; Mei trades type-castings for medicine for their father. A neighbor is arrested using information from the seized ledger, proving the stakes are real. POV: Xanthe. Beat: guilt hardens into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Knows
chapters.summary: Xanthe learns the ledger lists his own birth record—under a girl's name—alongside his father's old debts to rebel sympathizers. Exposure would mean prison or worse for the whole family. POV: Xanthe. Beat: invisibility revealed as always an illusion.

chapters.title: Deng's Bargain
chapters.summary: Deng offers to misfile key pages if Xanthe forges travel papers for him to flee north. They seal the pact over cheap liquor in the locked shop after curfew. POV: Deng. Beat: two liars finding honesty with each other.

chapters.title: Lanterns for the Dead
chapters.summary: Auntie Sable's workshop burns suspiciously; she survives but her tunnels are compromised. The town whispers that someone informed. POV: Xanthe. Beat: paranoia fractures the fragile alliance.

chapters.title: Mei's Choice
chapters.summary: Mei reveals she has been passing messages for the rebels for months and begs Xanthe to use the press for them properly. He refuses; they quarrel bitterly about survival versus sacrifice. POV: Mei. Beat: sibling rift mirrors the town's divide.

chapters.title: The Captain's Dinner
chapters.summary: Ruan summons the Zhou family to dine, probing their loyalty while quoting their own printed almanac back at them. Xanthe realizes Ruan suspects the ledger has been tampered with. POV: Xanthe. Beat: cat-and-mouse tension; the noose tightens.

chapters.title: Ice on the River
chapters.summary: The river freezes solid, halting boats and sealing the town. News arrives that the rebellion has reached the next province; Ruan doubles patrols and announces departures will be permitted only by military pass. POV: Deng. Beat: entrapment made physical.

chapters.title: The Forger's Hands
chapters.summary: Xanthe spends three nights forging passes, teaching Deng the craft as cover. Father Zhou collapses; the doctor says he needs treatment available only downstream. POV: Xanthe. Beat: love sharpened into desperation.

chapters.title: The Informer
chapters.summary: Deng identifies the informant: the shop's old apprentice, now Ruan's clerk. Confronting him, Xanthe learns the clerk sold names to feed his own mother. POV: Deng. Beat: the price of survival shown in its ugliest mirror.

chapters.title: Ashes and Type
chapters.summary: Ruan raids the shop and finds the forged passes' offcuts. Father Zhou takes the blame, claiming he acted alone, and is imprisoned. POV: Xanthe. Beat: devastating cost of the plan; grief and fury.

chapters.title: Breaking the Case
chapters.summary: Xanthe, Mei, Sable, and Deng plan a two-front rescue: free Father Zhou from the garrison jail and destroy the original ledger during the Lantern Festival, when fires mask everything. POV: alternating. Beat: the found family commits fully to each other.

chapters.title: The Night of Lanterns
chapters.summary: During the festival, Sable's lanterns ignite diversionary fires while Mei cuts the jail keys and Deng walks Ruan into a false report. The ledger burns in the press's own furnace. POV: Xanthe. Beat: triumphant chaos; the climax ignites.

chapters.title: What Fire Cannot Burn
chapters.summary: The escape goes wrong: Ruan corners Xanthe in the shop and recognizes what the ledger said about him. Deng intervenes, taking a bayonet wound; Ruan dies when the press house collapses in the fire. POV: Xanthe. Beat: victory purchased with blood.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: Rebel forces take the town; the ice groans toward breaking. One boat, one berth remains before spring. Father Zhou needs it; so does wounded Deng; Mei insists Xanthe take it himself. POV: Mei. Beat: the choice the whole book has built toward.

chapters.title: Which Family Gets Saved
chapters.summary: At the riverbank, Xanthe gives the berth to his father, telling him a son's duty is to stay with the town that raised him. Father Zhou, understanding everything at last, blesses both his children by their true names. POV: Xanthe. Beat: catharsis; identity claimed, not hidden.

chapters.title: Thaw
chapters.summary: The ice breaks; the boat carries Father Zhou downstream to safety. Xanthe, Mei, Sable, and recovering Deng reopen the print shop—not to hide, but to print freely. POV: Xanthe. Beat: belonging redefined as chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: When the Lantern Sings
chapters.summary: Months later, a letter arrives from Father Zhou, healed, enclosing a new typeface he carved: characters shaped like lantern flames. The shop prints its first free edition as Sable hangs lanterns that seem to hum in the wind. POV: Xanthe. Beat: peace earned, family found, voice finally his own.
